result: In 128 PASC vs 100 recovered controls, PASC had lower relative circulating cell-free mtDNA, higher CRP (25% low-grade inflammation) and worse cognition; ccf-mtDNA correlated positively with general cognition and negatively with CRP, but CRP differences did not survive confounder adjustment.
reason: Circulating cell-free mtDNA in long COVID (omics/mitochondria domain) is not covered; genetics-mr-biomarkers concerns genetically predicted mtDNA copy number, not measured ccf-mtDNA.

result: k-modes clustering of 19,019 DecodeME participants gave a high symptom burden cluster (57%) and lower burden cluster (43%); infectious and unknown onset had aOR 1.24 and 1.30 for high-burden membership vs non-infectious onset; no genetic variant was associated with cluster membership.
reason: Symptom-cluster phenotyping, not the GWAS loci/heritability claim; no atlas finding covers symptom clusters by onset type (genetics-infection-loci is about genetic correlation of onset groups, not symptom burden).

result: In 106 ME/CFS vs 91 controls (888 plasma metabolomic/lipidomic features), an Explainable Boosting Machine reached internal hold-out accuracy 0.909 and AUC 0.940 (0.882 without interaction terms); no external validation.
reason: Adds another internally validated metabolomic classifier consistent with high in-cohort performance, but it does not test external transfer, which is the finding's core claim, so it cannot replicate it.

result: An EBM classifier on plasma metabolomics/lipidomics reached AUC 0.940; indole-3-lactate featured only in a top pairwise interaction term with proline.
reason: No level or direction of indolelactate or other aromatic lactates is reported; an interaction feature in a classifier does not test the finding; paper already linked to omics-ml-classifiers.

result: In EPILOC (127 PCC vs 91 recovered controls, ~75 weeks post-infection), PCC had worse cognition and psychological distress; blood kynurenine, kynurenic acid and quinolinic acid showed group-specific associations, e.g. the KYNA/kynurenine ratio was negatively associated with general cognition in recovered controls (abstract text truncated).
reason: Measures peripheral kynurenine-pathway metabolites in long COVID with symptom links; a long COVID extension of the blood kynurenine question, though group-difference results are unclear in the garbled abstract.

result: In 39 long COVID vs 22 controls on tilt, the upright phase showed longer RR intervals, lower normalized LF, higher normalized HF and lower LF/HF in patients, with blunted pulse-pressure changes and no difference in baroreflex sensitivity.
reason: Same HRV measures, but the direction is opposite to the claimed lower HF/higher LF/HF; weak contradiction only, since it is long COVID, during tilt rather than at rest, and in normalized units.

result: Tilt testing in 39 long COVID vs 22 controls showed a blunted sympathetic HRV response upright (lower LF nu, lower LF/HF, p~0.03), attenuated pulse-pressure change on recovery (p<0.037), and normal baroreflex sensitivity.
reason: Objective tilt-based autonomic testing in long COVID finding abnormalities, but of a different kind (blunted sympathetic response, not POTS/initial OH prevalence) in a small sample, so it extends rather than replicates.

result: In 20 survivors of severe (hospitalised) COVID vs 20 matched controls at 18 and 24 months, patients had poorer sit-to-stand performance (mean difference 2.65) and higher Fatigue Severity Scale scores; fatigability results (torque, torque-time integral, RFD) are truncated in the abstract.
reason: Different method (dynamometer torque, not repeated handgrip) and population (post-hospitalisation severe COVID, not ME/CFS); the fatigability results are not visible in the truncated abstract, so too thin to link.

result: One year after Omicron infection, a 24-item symptom score was associated with long COVID vs antibody-verified never-infected controls (aOR 1.21 per point, 95% CI 1.13-1.30); patients reported fatigue, cognitive impairment and more intercurrent infections.
reason: The truncated abstract gives no cognitive test, domain or effect size, so it cannot be checked against the domain-specific ME/CFS deficit claim; too thin.

result: In 108 patients with post-COVID headache and/or brain fog vs symptom-free post-COVID controls, anterior Focal Cerebral Arteriopathy Severity Score rose with symptom categories (combined 6.6 vs headache 3.6 vs brain fog 4.7 vs control 0.8), suggesting anterior circulation arteriopathy and hypoperfusion in brain fog.
reason: Intracranial arteriopathy scoring in long COVID (neuro/vascular domain) is not covered; neuro-cbf-rest concerns resting CBF in ME/CFS, not vessel arteriopathy.
